dial.summary: The July 23 10-year TIPS auction cleared at 2.438% real yield—highest since October 2008—and CME FedWatch puts a 36% probability on a Fed hike at tomorrow's July 29 FOMC decision, making real yields and DXY (101.52) the dominant headwinds; yet TOTAL holds near $2.28T, BTC.D remains firm at 56.3%, perp funding is a supportive +0.004%/8h, and stablecoin dominance is declining at 13.2%, keeping the BTC Accumulation thesis intact pending Chair Warsh's guidance tomorrow.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: MacroMicro 4-bank aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) holds at $102,653B (~$102.7T) per May 2026 vintage—June and July data not yet published; US M2 reached an all-time high of $22.7T in February 2026 and continues to expand; China M2 YoY growth ~9%; EU M2 ~$18.6T; 4-week trend up (uptrend sustained across components, YoY growth positive); status supportive (expanding 4-week trend; YoY contracting headwind not met).

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: June 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI confirmed at 53.3% (released July 1)—sixth consecutive expansion month, down 0.7pp from May's 54.0%; July 2026 print releases August 3 at 10:00 AM ET; June sub-indicators: new orders 56.0%, prices paid 73.0% (largest single-month drop since July 2022), employment 49.7% (contracting); 4-week trend down (54.0% → 53.3%); status neutral (above 50 but falling—supportive requires above 50 AND rising).

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY spot at 101.52 on July 28, 2026 (up from 101.18 on July 27); June 30 close at ~101.34; 4-week change: (101.52 − 101.34) / 101.34 = +0.18%—within the <0.5% relative flat threshold; CME FedWatch shows 36% probability of a Fed hike at tomorrow's July 29 FOMC decision, a near-term upside catalyst; status headwind (above the 100 ICE DXY threshold; supportive requires below 97.5).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: July 23, 2026 10-year TIPS reopening auction (CUSIP 91282CRE3) cleared at a real yield of 2.438%—highest at auction since October 2008 per tipswatch.com; bid-to-cover of 2.30 indicates weak demand; 4-week trend up: real yield rose approximately +0.26pp from ~2.18% (June 25) to 2.44% (July 23 auction); status headwind (above 2% and rising on 4-week basis; a July 29 FOMC hold with dovish guidance is the primary compression catalyst).

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: 10-year Treasury at 4.69%, 2-year at 4.33% (July 24, 2026 close per AdvisorPerspectives); spread: 4.69% − 4.33% = +0.36%; 4-week trend flat: spread narrowed ~4bps from ~+0.40% (late June) to +0.36%—within the flat threshold; a Fed hike at July 29 FOMC would likely flatten or briefly invert the curve; status neutral (positive spread clear of the −50bps deep-inversion headwind; not steepening on 30-day basis).

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL at $6.75T for week ending July 22, 2026 (H.4.1 released July 23 per Convex/FRED); next H.4.1 release July 30, 2026 (covering week ending July 29); 4-week trend flat: balance sheet moved from ~$6.72T (late June) to $6.75T (+0.45%), within the flat threshold; status supportive (flat to marginally growing; no aggressive QT with rising overnight rates).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: CoinGlass, The Block, and Coinalyze all proxy-blocked this run (HTTP 403); value carried forward unchanged from July 27 run at +0.004%/8h (annualized ~+4.4%)—well below the 0.04%/8h overheating threshold; 30-day trend held down from ~+0.006%/8h (late June); status supportive (near-zero funding consistent with spot-led price action, far from overheating).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$304B (USDT ~$186B + USDC ~$75B lead per July 2026 sources); total crypto market ~$2.30T; dominance: $304B / $2.30T = 13.2%, down from 13.3% prior run; 30-day trend down: stablecoin supply contracted from ~$314B (late June) as capital rotated into risk assets; status supportive (30-day downtrend intact; rising-dominance-with-rising-TOTAL headwind condition not met—TOTAL approximately flat to slightly up).

upcoming.title: FOMC Rate Decision & Press Conference (July 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve rate decision at 2:00 PM ET, Chair Warsh press conference at 2:30 PM ET—non-SEP meeting (no dot plot); current target range 3.5–3.75%; CME FedWatch shows 64% hold / 36% hike probability as of July 27, with renewed uncertainty driven by energy-price volatility and the July 23 TIPS auction at 2.438% (highest real yield at auction since Oct 2008); a hold with dovish guidance could push DXY below 100 and compress real yields; a hike would be the most hawkish FOMC surprise in years.

upcoming.title: Q2 GDP Advance Estimate / June PCE / BOE Rate Decision / Jobless Claims / WALCL H.4.1
upcoming.note: BEA Q2 2026 GDP Advance Estimate at 8:30 AM ET—first official read on Q2 economic growth; BEA Personal Income and Outlays (June PCE) at 8:30 AM ET—core PCE is the Fed's preferred inflation gauge and the first major inflation read after the July 29 FOMC decision; Initial Jobless Claims (week ended July 26) at 8:30 AM ET; Bank of England MPC decision at 12:00 BST (Super Thursday with full Monetary Policy Report, Bank Rate currently 3.75%); WALCL H.4.1 (week ending July 29) at 4:30 PM ET.

upcoming.title: BOJ Rate Decision / Employment Cost Index Q2 / UMich Final Sentiment (July 2026)
upcoming.note: Bank of Japan monetary policy statement released overnight ET (concluding July 30–31 BOJ meeting)—Policy Rate currently 0.75% (highest since 1995); BOJ will assess whether JPY dynamics and global disinflation justify further normalization in light of the post-FOMC July 29 outcome; Employment Cost Index Q2 2026 at 8:30 AM ET (BLS)—Fed's preferred quarterly labor cost measure; University of Michigan Final Consumer Sentiment (July 2026) at 10:00 AM ET—final 1-year and 5-year inflation expectations.

upcoming.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI (July 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM® Manufacturing PMI® for July 2026 at 10:00 AM ET—first major Q3 manufacturing activity read and the first significant macro release after the July 29 FOMC decision; prior June reading: 53.3% (sixth consecutive expansion month, down 0.7pp from May's 54.0%); markets will watch whether expansion continues above 50, whether new orders (June: 56.0%) hold momentum, and whether prices paid (June: 73.0%) continues its disinflationary path; a fall toward or below 50% would raise late-cycle caution.

upcoming.title: JOLTS Job Openings (June 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS) for June 2026 at 10:00 AM ET—job openings are a key Fed metric for measuring labor demand tightness; arriving the day after the August 3 ISM Manufacturing print and 6 days after the July 29 FOMC decision, this will contribute to the September 15–16 SEP FOMC narrative on whether the labor market is softening in line with the soft-landing thesis.
